chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Abdillah, from Ali ibn al-Malik, from Bakkar ibn al-Jarrah, from Bistam, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

From breastfeeding, only the womb (stomach) from which one nursed becomes prohibited. The correct interpretation of this report is that the prohibition does not extend to those related to the mother via breastfeeding, because such a person is only related to another womb, and what is specific to her womb by birth is what becomes prohibited. It is also possible that this was stated as precautionary piency (taqiyyah), because among the jurists is one who says that the prohibition does not extend beyond the two nursing individuals.

key_terms.الْبَطْن: Womb/Stomach (referring to the source of nourishment)

ai.seo_question: Does breastfeeding create a mahram relationship for all relatives of the nursing mother?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies that the prohibition of marriage due to breastfeeding (radha') is strictly limited to the direct nursing dyad (the infant and the wet nurse) and does not extend to her other relatives, as they are not connected via the same 'womb' of nourishment. The text notes a scholarly divergence, with some jurists interpreting this limited scope as *taqiyyah* (precautionary piety) to be safe, while others maintain it as the definitive ruling, reflecting the nuanced development of Shia fiqh on kinship ties.
